phases.title: Gradebook schema — add a single scores table to db/schema.ts, generate + apply migration
preconditions: Phase 1 complete — test:db plumbing is fixed
MANDATORY: Confirm DATABASE_URL in .env.local does NOT point at the production database before running db:generate or db:migrate. If you cannot confirm this, stop and report — do not run migrations.
testsFirst: No separate test file for schema shape — the .db.test.ts in phase 3 exercises the tables. Confirm schema.ts compiles: RUN: npx tsc --noEmit (must pass before opening a migration)
implementationSteps: DECISION (2026-06-27): The original plan had two tables (attempts + scores) in a 1→many relationship. This was collapsed to a SINGLE 'scores' table. Rationale verified against code: features/gradebook/server/aggregation.ts (computeSubjectGrade, masteryStatus, decayStatus) operates on a FLAT Score[] and never groups by attempt; the Attempt.scores grouping in types.ts is never exercised. The separate attempts table only duplicated householdId/learnerId/subjectId/occurredAt onto scores with no consumer. One graded data point = one scores row. If a real rubric feature (multiple scored dimensions per assessment event) ever lands, reintroduce attempts as an additive migration then — do not pre-build it (YAGNI).
In db/schema.ts, after the portfolioEvidence table block, add ONE table:

Table 'scores': id text PK, householdId text notNull references households.id, learnerId text notNull references learners.id, subjectId text nullable references subjects.id, lessonTaskId text nullable references lessonTasks.id, state text notNull default 'not_graded' (values: graded|not_graded|missing|excused|complete), numericValue numeric nullable (precision 5 scale 2), source text notNull default 'parent' (values: auto|parent|publisher|outside|ai), occurredAt timestamp notNull, comment text nullable, createdAt timestamp notNull, updatedAt timestamp notNull. Indexes: index('scores_household_learner_subject_idx').on(householdId, learnerId, subjectId), index('scores_lesson_task_idx').on(lessonTaskId). NOTE: no attemptId column and no attempts table — they were removed per the DECISION above.

Also add nullable columns to the existing 'subjects' table (ALTER equivalent — add fields at the end of the subjects pgTable definition): gradingScaleId text nullable (no FK in v1 — grading_scales table is out of scope for Layer 3 MVP), aggregationRuleId text nullable (same), isFormalCourse boolean notNull default false, creditHours numeric nullable (precision 4 scale 2), termModel text nullable. All nullable or have defaults — no backfill needed.

COMPOSITE FK PREP (parent tables): the scores table will reference learners, subjects, and lessonTasks via composite (id, householdId) foreign keys so a score can never point at a parent in a different household. A composite FK must target a PK or UNIQUE constraint, so first add a composite UNIQUE to each of those three EXISTING tables: in each table's (t) => [...] array add unique('learners_id_household_uq').on(t.id, t.householdId) / unique('subjects_id_household_uq').on(t.id, t.householdId) / unique('lesson_tasks_id_household_uq').on(t.id, t.householdId). This is ADDITIVE and CANNOT fail validation — (id) is already the PK, so (id, householdId) is trivially unique. Import `unique` from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core' if not already imported.

COMPOSITE FKs (scores): in the scores (t) => [...] array, add composite FKs using the foreignKey() helper (import { foreignKey } from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core'): foreignKey({ columns: [t.learnerId, t.householdId], foreignColumns: [learners.id, learners.householdId], name: 'scores_learner_household_fk' }); foreignKey({ columns: [t.subjectId, t.householdId], foreignColumns: [subjects.id, subjects.householdId], name: 'scores_subject_household_fk' }); foreignKey({ columns: [t.lessonTaskId, t.householdId], foreignColumns: [lessonTasks.id, lessonTasks.householdId], name: 'scores_lesson_task_household_fk' }). Do NOT also declare a plain .references() on learnerId/subjectId/lessonTaskId — the composite FK replaces it. Keep householdId → households.id as a simple .references() (households has no householdId column). Nullable columns (subjectId, lessonTaskId) use Postgres default MATCH SIMPLE: the FK is only enforced when the column is non-null, so optional links still work.

Run: npm run db:generate — this should produce exactly one new migration file (e.g. 0020_gradebook_core.sql). Verify the generated SQL adds the single scores table (with the three composite FKs), the five new columns on subjects, and the composite UNIQUE constraints on learners/subjects/lessonTasks (NOT an attempts table). Do not edit the generated SQL.
Run: npm run db:migrate — apply to the non-prod database pointed at by .env.local DATABASE_URL.
doneWhen: RUN: npx tsc --noEmit (no type errors)
RUN: npm run db:generate (one new migration file produced, no schema drift)
RUN: npm run db:migrate (applies cleanly — the parent UNIQUE adds and composite FKs validate, since all new tables are empty and the parent UNIQUE is a superset of the existing PK)
RUN: npm run build (build passes)
phases.writeBack: Record the migration file number/name produced (e.g. 0020_gradebook_core.sql). Record that subjects table now has gradingScaleId, aggregationRuleId, isFormalCourse, creditHours, termModel columns. Confirm a single scores table was created (no attempts table) with composite (id, householdId) FKs to learners/subjects/lessonTasks, and that learners/subjects/lessonTasks gained a composite UNIQUE(id, householdId). Phase 3 depends on scores existing.

phases.title: Compliance schema — add 5 compliance tables to db/schema.ts, generate + apply migration
preconditions: Phase 3 complete — gradebook repo tests pass
MANDATORY: Confirm DATABASE_URL in .env.local does NOT point at production before running db:generate or db:migrate.
testsFirst: RUN: npx tsc --noEmit (must pass before generating migration)
implementationSteps: In db/schema.ts, after the scores table block, add these five tables:

Table 'compliance_rulesets': id text PK, state text notNull, pathwayKey text notNull, requirementType text notNull, value numeric nullable (precision 8 scale 2), unit text notNull default 'days', sourceUrl text nullable, lastVerifiedAt timestamp nullable, isVerified boolean notNull default false, createdAt timestamp notNull, updatedAt timestamp notNull. Index: index('compliance_rulesets_state_pathway_idx').on(state, pathwayKey). NOTE: no householdId — these are platform-wide reference rows seeded from docs/compliance-research/.

Table 'household_compliance_config': householdId text PK references households.id, activeRulesetId text nullable references compliance_rulesets.id, pathwayKey text nullable, updatedAt timestamp notNull. (Single row per household — householdId is the PK.)

Table 'compliance_overrides': id text PK, householdId text notNull references households.id, schoolYearId text notNull references school_years.id, requirementType text notNull, overrideValue numeric notNull (precision 8 scale 2), reason text nullable, appliedAt timestamp notNull, createdAt timestamp notNull, updatedAt timestamp notNull. Index: index('compliance_overrides_household_year_idx').on(householdId, schoolYearId).

Table 'compliance_deadlines': id text PK, householdId text notNull references households.id, schoolYearId text notNull references school_years.id, label text notNull, dueDate date notNull, isCompleted boolean notNull default false, requirementType text notNull, createdAt timestamp notNull, updatedAt timestamp notNull. Index: index('compliance_deadlines_household_year_idx').on(householdId, schoolYearId).

Table 'compliance_submissions': id text PK, householdId text notNull references households.id, schoolYearId text notNull references school_years.id, status text notNull default 'drafted' (values: drafted|sent|accepted), submittedAt timestamp nullable, acceptedAt timestamp nullable, snapshotJson jsonb nullable, createdAt timestamp notNull, updatedAt timestamp notNull. Index: index('compliance_submissions_household_year_idx').on(householdId, schoolYearId).

COMPOSITE FK PREP: compliance_overrides, compliance_deadlines, and compliance_submissions each carry householdId AND schoolYearId. Add a composite UNIQUE to the EXISTING schoolYears table so it can be a composite-FK target: in its (t) => [...] array add unique('school_years_id_household_uq').on(t.id, t.householdId). Additive, cannot fail (id is already PK).

COMPOSITE FKs: for EACH of compliance_overrides, compliance_deadlines, compliance_submissions, replace the plain schoolYearId .references(() => schoolYears.id) with a composite FK in the (t) => [...] array: foreignKey({ columns: [t.schoolYearId, t.householdId], foreignColumns: [schoolYears.id, schoolYears.householdId], name: '<table>_school_year_household_fk' }). Keep householdId → households.id as a simple .references(). NOTE: compliance_rulesets is platform-wide (no householdId) so it gets no composite FK; household_compliance_config.activeRulesetId → compliance_rulesets.id stays a simple FK (rulesets are not tenant-scoped).
Run: npm run db:generate — produces one new migration for the 5 compliance tables (plus the schoolYears composite UNIQUE). Verify the SQL. Do not edit it.
Run: npm run db:migrate — apply to the non-prod DB.
doneWhen: RUN: npx tsc --noEmit
RUN: npm run db:generate (one new migration produced)
RUN: npm run db:migrate (applies cleanly)
RUN: npm run build
phases.writeBack: Record migration file name. Tables compliance_rulesets, household_compliance_config, compliance_overrides, compliance_deadlines, compliance_submissions now exist; the three household+schoolYear tables use composite (schoolYearId, householdId) FKs to schoolYears, which gained a composite UNIQUE(id, householdId). Phase 5 depends on all five.

phases.title: Badges schema — add 5 badge tables to db/schema.ts, generate + apply migration
preconditions: Phase 5 complete — compliance repo tests pass
MANDATORY: Confirm DATABASE_URL in .env.local does NOT point at production before running db:generate or db:migrate.
testsFirst: RUN: npx tsc --noEmit (must pass before generating migration)
implementationSteps: In db/schema.ts, after the compliance_submissions table block, add these five tables:

Table 'badge_definitions': id text PK, householdId text nullable references households.id (null = platform starter badge), title text notNull, description text notNull, criteria text notNull, emblemKey text notNull, gradeBands jsonb notNull default '[]', verificationRequirement text notNull default 'none' (values: none|parent|external), isStarter boolean notNull default false, enabled boolean notNull default true, visibility text notNull default 'household' (values: household|platform), createdAt timestamp notNull, updatedAt timestamp notNull. Index: index('badge_definitions_household_idx').on(householdId) (nullable index is fine).

Table 'badge_awards': id text PK, householdId text notNull references households.id, learnerId text notNull references learners.id, badgeId text notNull references badge_definitions.id, status text notNull default 'draft' (values: draft|submitted|verified), submittedAt timestamp nullable, verifiedAt timestamp nullable, approvedAt timestamp nullable, createdAt timestamp notNull, updatedAt timestamp notNull. Indexes: index('badge_awards_household_learner_idx').on(householdId, learnerId), index('badge_awards_badge_idx').on(badgeId).

Table 'badge_award_evidence': id text PK, householdId text notNull references households.id, badgeAwardId text notNull references badge_awards.id (onDelete: 'cascade'), evidenceId text notNull references portfolio_evidence.id, addedAt timestamp notNull. Index: index('badge_award_evidence_award_idx').on(badgeAwardId).

Table 'badge_settings': householdId text PK references households.id (onDelete: 'cascade'), platformBadgesEnabled boolean notNull default true, createdAt timestamp notNull, updatedAt timestamp notNull.

Table 'autonomy_unlocks': id text PK, householdId text notNull references households.id, learnerId text notNull references learners.id, badgeId text notNull references badge_definitions.id, unlockedAt timestamp notNull, grantedBy text notNull, createdAt timestamp notNull. Index: index('autonomy_unlocks_household_learner_idx').on(householdId, learnerId).

COMPOSITE FK PREP: add a composite UNIQUE to the EXISTING portfolioEvidence table — unique('portfolio_evidence_id_household_uq').on(t.id, t.householdId) — so badge_award_evidence can composite-reference it. Additive, cannot fail. Also add unique('badge_awards_id_household_uq').on(t.id, t.householdId) to the NEW badge_awards table (zero rows, free) so badge_award_evidence can composite-reference the award.

COMPOSITE FKs: badge_awards — replace the plain learnerId .references() with foreignKey({ columns: [t.learnerId, t.householdId], foreignColumns: [learners.id, learners.householdId], name: 'badge_awards_learner_household_fk' }). autonomy_unlocks — same composite (learnerId, householdId) → learners. badge_award_evidence — add foreignKey({ columns: [t.badgeAwardId, t.householdId], foreignColumns: [badgeAwards.id, badgeAwards.householdId], name: 'badge_award_evidence_award_household_fk' }) AND foreignKey({ columns: [t.evidenceId, t.householdId], foreignColumns: [portfolioEvidence.id, portfolioEvidence.householdId], name: 'badge_award_evidence_evidence_household_fk' }), replacing the plain references on those columns. Keep householdId → households.id as a simple .references() on every table.

DELIBERATE EXCEPTION — badgeId stays a SIMPLE FK: badge_awards.badgeId, autonomy_unlocks.badgeId, and badge_award_evidence (none) reference badge_definitions.id with a plain .references(). Do NOT make badgeId a composite (badgeId, householdId) FK, because badge_definitions.householdId is NULLABLE (null = platform starter badge): a household's award legitimately references a platform badge whose householdId is null, so a composite match would be impossible. Tenant integrity for badgeId is enforced at the repository layer instead (listBadgeDefinitions already scopes to householdId-null-or-own). Note this in a code comment on the badgeId column.
Run: npm run db:generate — produces one new migration for the 5 badge tables (plus the portfolioEvidence composite UNIQUE). Verify the SQL.
Run: npm run db:migrate — apply to the non-prod DB.
doneWhen: RUN: npx tsc --noEmit
RUN: npm run db:generate (one new migration produced)
RUN: npm run db:migrate (applies cleanly)
RUN: npm run build

phases.title: Lesson Planner — lesson_steps schema + migration + repository CRUD + .db.test.ts
preconditions: Phase 7 complete — badge repo tests pass
MANDATORY: Confirm DATABASE_URL in .env.local does NOT point at production before running db:generate or db:migrate.
testsFirst: Write the .db.test.ts BEFORE implementing the repository functions (tests will fail until implementation is done):
NEW features/plan/__tests__/integration/lesson-steps.db.test.ts:

Test 'createLessonStep + listLessonSteps round-trip': insert a lesson_task row first (use existing lessonTasks table), then createLessonStep({lessonTaskId, order:1, stepText:'Read pages 1-5', type:'reading'}), then listLessonSteps(lessonTaskId) — expect 1 step.
Test 'listLessonSteps is ordered by order column': createLessonStep order:2, createLessonStep order:1, createLessonStep order:3 — listLessonSteps must return [1,2,3].
Test 'updateLessonStep changes stepText': createLessonStep, updateLessonStep(id, lessonTaskId, {stepText:'Updated text'}), listLessonSteps — expect updated text.
Test 'deleteLessonStep removes the row': createLessonStep, deleteLessonStep(id, lessonTaskId), listLessonSteps — expect empty array.
Use real DB. Unique scoped IDs. afterEach cleanup including lesson_tasks row.
implementationSteps: In db/schema.ts, after the autonomy_unlocks table block, add table 'lesson_steps': id text PK, lessonTaskId text notNull references lessonTasks.id (onDelete: 'cascade'), order integer notNull default 0, stepText text notNull, type text notNull default 'instruction' (values: instruction|reading|practice|discussion|assessment), doneCriteria text nullable, quantity integer nullable, createdAt timestamp notNull, updatedAt timestamp notNull. Index: index('lesson_steps_lesson_task_idx').on(lessonTaskId).

NO COMPOSITE FK HERE (deliberate): lesson_steps does NOT carry householdId — it is a leaf child always reached through its lessonTask, which is tenant-scoped. A simple lessonTaskId → lessonTasks.id FK with onDelete:'cascade' is correct; tenant isolation is inherited via the parent task. Repository reads/writes scope by lessonTaskId (see updateLessonStep/deleteLessonStep guarding on id AND lessonTaskId). Do not add householdId just to enable a composite FK.
Run: npm run db:generate — produces one new migration for lesson_steps. Verify SQL. Do not edit it.
Run: npm run db:migrate.

Add to features/plan/server/repository.ts: import { lessonSteps } from '@/db/schema' alongside the existing import of lessonTasks. Add these types: export type LessonStepRow = typeof lessonSteps.$inferSelect; export interface CreateLessonStepInput { lessonTaskId: string; order: number; stepText: string; type?: string; doneCriteria?: string; quantity?: number }; export interface UpdateLessonStepInput { order?: number; stepText?: string; type?: string; doneCriteria?: string | null; quantity?: number | null }.

Add: export async function listLessonSteps(lessonTaskId: string): Promise<LessonStepRow[]> — db.select().from(lessonSteps).where(eq(lessonSteps.lessonTaskId, lessonTaskId)).orderBy(lessonSteps.order).
Add: export async function createLessonStep(input: CreateLessonStepInput): Promise<LessonStepRow> — insert with id:`step_${Date.now()}_${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2,7)}`.

Add: export async function updateLessonStep(id: string, lessonTaskId: string, patch: UpdateLessonStepInput): Promise<LessonStepRow | null> — update where id AND lessonTaskId (prevents cross-task mutation), return updated row or null.
Add: export async function deleteLessonStep(id: string, lessonTaskId: string): Promise<boolean> — delete where id AND lessonTaskId, return true if a row was deleted.

RUN: npm test
RUN: npm run build

phases.title: Reference data seed — compliance_rulesets + starter badge_definitions from JSON research file
preconditions: Phases 4 and 6 complete — compliance_rulesets and badge_definitions tables exist
testsFirst: No automated test for the seed script itself — idempotency is verified by running it twice (doneWhen check). The seed is a script, not a library function. Verify correctness by running and inspecting output.
implementationSteps: Create scripts/seed-reference-data.ts. This is an idempotent reference-data seeder — it inserts platform-wide rows with stable deterministic IDs using ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. It must NEVER truncate existing rows.
Guard at top: if (!process.env.DATABASE_URL) { console.error('DATABASE_URL not set'); process.exit(1) }

COMPLIANCE RULESETS: Read docs/compliance-research/homeschool-requirements-2026-06-27.json (import fs/path, JSON.parse). For each state entry in the array, for each pathway within it, for each requirement key (instructionDaysPerYear, instructionHoursPerYear, requiredSubjects, filings, evaluationOrTesting, recordRetention), generate a stable deterministic ID: `ruleset_${state.state.toLowerCase()}_${pathway.key}_${requirementKey}` (e.g. 'ruleset_tx_private-school-exemption_instructionDaysPerYear'). Map to compliance_rulesets row: { id, state: state.state, pathwayKey: pathway.key, requirementType: requirementKey, value: req.value is a number ? req.value : null, unit: (requirementKey.includes('Hour') ? 'hours' : requirementKey === 'requiredSubjects' ? 'subjects' : 'days'), sourceUrl: req.source_url ?? null, lastVerifiedAt: req.verified && state.last_verified ? new Date(state.last_verified) : null, isVerified: req.verified === true, createdAt: now, updatedAt: now }. Insert all rows via a single db.insert(complianceRulesets).values([...rows]).onConflictDoNothing(). Log count of rows attempted.

STARTER BADGE DEFINITIONS: Define a static inline array of 8 starter badges (do not read from file — badge data is not in the compliance JSON). Use stable IDs prefixed 'badge_starter_': badge_starter_quran_memorizer, badge_starter_math_champion, badge_starter_avid_reader, badge_starter_science_explorer, badge_starter_history_detective, badge_starter_creative_writer, badge_starter_language_learner, badge_starter_community_helper. Each has: { id, householdId: null, title, description, criteria, emblemKey (same as id suffix, e.g. 'quran_memorizer'), gradeBands: ['g1_4','g5_8','g9_12'], verificationRequirement: 'parent', isStarter: true, enabled: true, visibility: 'platform', createdAt: now, updatedAt: now }. Insert via db.insert(badgeDefinitions).values([...badges]).onConflictDoNothing(). Log count.
Add 'db:seed:reference' script to package.json scripts: 'dotenv -e .env.local -- tsx scripts/seed-reference-data.ts'.

The script must print a clear summary: 'Inserted N compliance_rulesets rows (M already existed)' — use the returning() count vs attempted count to calculate. Alternatively log 'Attempted N rows, onConflictDoNothing applied — re-run is a no-op'.
doneWhen: RUN: npm run db:seed:reference (first run — expect rows inserted, no errors)
RUN: npm run db:seed:reference (second run — same command, expect 0 rows inserted / no-op confirmed by log)
RUN: npm run build (seed script should not affect build, but verify it compiles)
Manually inspect: connect to DB (npm run db:studio or psql) and confirm compliance_rulesets has rows for TX and FL (minimum), and badge_definitions has 8 starter rows with householdId null.
phases.writeBack: Reference seed script created at scripts/seed-reference-data.ts. db:seed:reference added to package.json. Idempotency confirmed by running twice. Record how many compliance_rulesets rows were inserted and which states are covered. NOTE: rows where requirementType is 'requiredSubjects' will have value:null in the DB even though the JSON contains a string array — the seeder intentionally discards non-numeric values since the column is numeric; the authoritative subject list is reachable via sourceUrl.

phases.title: Demo seed extension — add gradebook, compliance, and badge rows to the demo households
preconditions: Phases 2, 4, 6, 8 complete — all new tables are migrated
Phase 9 complete — reference seed has inserted compliance_rulesets and starter badge_definitions
DATABASE_URL points at a non-prod database (mandatory — never run demo seed against prod)
testsFirst: No separate test. Verify via running: npm run db:seed:demo (must succeed on an empty DB). Then run npm run db:seed:reference first if needed (rulesets + badges must exist for FK references in badge_awards). Then run npm run db:seed:demo.
implementationSteps: Read scripts/seed/buildPayload.ts to understand the existing payload structure (what tables it builds rows for, how it returns the payload object). Do not modify the build strategy — only ADD new fields to the payload object and new rows to the existing build loops.

Read scripts/seed/loadPayload.ts to understand how chunks are inserted (db.insert(...).values(chunk).onConflictDoNothing()). Add new insert blocks for the new tables at the end of loadDemoSeedPayload(), after all existing inserts.

In buildPayload.ts, for each demo household's learners + subjects, generate 4-8 score rows per learner per subject spread over the 150-day history (state:'graded', numericValue: random 70-100, source:'parent', occurredAt within the window). Use counter-based IDs not Date.now() (to avoid collisions in bulk build): e.g. `score_demo_${householdIdx}_${learnerIdx}_${subjectIdx}_${n}`. Missing/excused: include ~10% of scores as state:'excused' with numericValue:null to exercise the no-zero guarantee. NOTE: there is no attempts table — scores are inserted directly (lessonTaskId may be left null for demo data).

Add 1-3 compliance_deadline rows per demo household per school year (e.g. 'Annual notification', 'Portfolio submission', 'Year-end assessment') with realistic dueDate values within the school year. These are household-specific deadline rows (not rulesets). IDs: `deadline_demo_${householdIdx}_${n}`.

Add badge_awards for 2-3 of the 8 starter badges per learner in demo households. Status:'verified', approvedAt: a date within the 150-day history. badgeId must reference the starter badge IDs seeded by seed-reference-data.ts (e.g. 'badge_starter_avid_reader'). NOTE: load db:seed:reference BEFORE db:seed:demo for FK integrity. IDs: `award_demo_${householdIdx}_${learnerIdx}_${badgeIdx}`.

In loadPayload.ts, add insert blocks: db.insert(scores).values(chunk).onConflictDoNothing() (chunked at 200 rows); db.insert(complianceDeadlines).values(chunk).onConflictDoNothing() (chunked at 50); db.insert(badgeAwards).values(chunk).onConflictDoNothing() (chunked at 100). There is no attempts insert — the attempts table was removed.
Update summarizePayload() to include counts for the new tables so the console output shows them.

IMPORTANT: badge_awards reference badge_definitions rows that are inserted by seed-reference-data.ts, not by the demo seed itself. The demo seed loadPayload must run AFTER db:seed:reference or FK inserts will fail. Add a log warning at the top of loadPayload if it detects badge_definitions is empty: 'WARNING: badge_definitions is empty — run npm run db:seed:reference before npm run db:seed:demo for badge award rows to succeed'.

RUN: npm run db:seed:demo (on a fresh/empty DB — should complete without FK errors)
Verify console output shows score, compliance_deadline, and badge_award counts > 0
